title: The Chief AI Officer: Scientist, Architect, Coach — Rania Khalaf, WSO2
talk_summary: A chief AI officer at WSO2 describes her role as a mix of scientist, architect, and coach, and how the balance shifts by company type and AI maturity. She covers what she measures (AI fluency, adoption depth, tool availability, GEO visibility) and why she rejects token counts as a metric.

takeaways.technique: Measure adoption depth, not token volume
takeaways.what_they_do: She explicitly refuses to measure tokens because the metric is easily gamed, and instead tracks whether teams move from simple tasks (email cleanup, code completion) to reworked workflows and instantiated agentic employees.
takeaways.evidence_quote: someone asked me to measure tokens ... and I said no ... it's so easily hackable

takeaways.technique: Distributed AI leads per product instead of central bottleneck
takeaways.what_they_do: A small central AI team works with everyone, but every product team has its own AI lead and builders, so requests don't queue behind a center of excellence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have an AI lead in every single product and every product team has folks working on the AI capabilities

takeaways.technique: Make every product agent-consumable (MCP + CLI + skills)
takeaways.what_they_do: They require every product to expose an MCP server, skills, and CLI, and docs to be LLM-consumable, so agents can operate the product directly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this year we're making sure every product can be used by agents. So everything needs to have an MCP server and skills and CLI

takeaways.technique: Right-size the technique to the problem
takeaways.what_they_do: When scientists wanted AI for embryo sizing, she used simple blob detection instead of ML because the task didn't need a model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just need like blob detection you don't need any machine learning ... we use a very simple algorithm and it worked really well

takeaways.what_they_do: She warns that forcing internal use of your own product is worthless if nobody acts on the feedback; the loop must feed back into the product.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they make us use our product ... except nobody takes any feedback ... hopefully we close the feedback loop
